chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
If he divorces her for the waiting period more than once, the advantage (of revocability) over one divorce is not [applicable to] a single divorce [in the same way].
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband pronounces divorce multiple times during the wife's waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the Shia juristic position that multiple divorces pronounced within a single waiting period ('iddah) do not accumulate to become three distinct divorces, but rather remain as one, thereby preserving the wife's right to return to her husband without a intervening marriage (nikah mubarram). This ruling contrasts with the Hanafi view of 'talqat al-wahid' (single pronouncement counting as three) and aligns with the interpretation that the 'iddah period is a single legal unit for the purpose of revocability. The term 'fadl' here refers to the legal advantage or distinct status of the divorce count, emphasizing that the husband does not gain the benefit of a completed triple divorce until the 'iddah expires.
